why: The whole point of issue #260's store is that the pane's choices survive a reload. Without this write the pane still LOOKS correct for the rest of the page-session -- every selection renders, Start carries it, the gate runs -- and forgets everything on the next load. That is invisible to any assertion made against a single HUD instance, which is why the persistence tests read back through a SECOND createHud over the same Storage. Re-measured at hud.navigation.test.ts once #318's layer cases joined the file: the callback-and-store sweep's negative control expects a role click to write exactly once. Pinned by name since the hud suite was split (issue #511); its killers live in hud.navigation.test.ts, hud.versus-setup.test.ts. Two roving-tabindex cases it named until issue #1093 are not killers: in the 150-test `hud.navigation.test.ts` they failed only because each retained-setup case that builds its own HUD fails under this mutation before its own `dispose`, and the HUD it leaves listening on `window` took later key presses in that file (measured the same with the display cache and without). Split into `hud.roving.test.ts`, they pass.
killedBy: hud: navigation layers -- origin, Back and focus restoration (issue #318) Back fires no start, pick, reset, quit, pause, setup or open callback, leaves no reset armed, and writes nothing to the retained VS store
hud: the versus pane reads and writes the RETAINED setup (issue #260) never writes a device to storage -- only the role pattern survives
hud: the versus pane reads and writes the RETAINED setup (issue #260) persists a role choice to the RAW key, so a second HUD on the same storage opens with it
hud: the versus pane reads and writes the RETAINED setup (issue #260) persists the match rules too, not only the slots -- every write goes through one funnel
